trust_decision.summary: migration:generate decides how schema-builder SQL text (which carries DB-introspected comments/defaults) is embedded in a JS template literal in the generated migration file; at the pinned commit only backticks are escaped, so backslashes and ${...} pass into executable code.

landing_point.why: The summary names migration:generate and template literals; the only template-literal construction of queries is the upQuery/downQuery replaceAll("`") lines in this handler.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `typeorm migration:generate <path>` (up queries), TS and JS (-o/--esm) templates
new helper escapeTemplateLiteral called by both sites above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both commits are the same change backported to two branches; every changed source line is in src/commands/MigrationGenerateCommand.ts.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the SQL is generated by TypeORM itself and comments are already SQL-escaped by escapeComment (src/driver/postgres/PostgresQueryRunner.ts:5091-5099), so only backticks need escaping, or could escape `${` alone and leave backslash handling out as cosmetic.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate SQL containing MySQL backtick identifiers, backslashes (MySQL comment escaping doubles them) and literal `$` must come out byte-identical when the migration runs; the expected templates assert the exact \` output form, so dropping/rejecting such characters or switching to another quoting style breaks generation tests.

O7_producer.where: driver schema builder log(): dataSource.driver.createSchemaBuilder().log() at src/commands/MigrationGenerateCommand.ts:99-101; comment text escaped for SQL only in src/driver/postgres/PostgresQueryRunner.ts:5091-5099 and src/driver/mysql/MysqlQueryRunner.ts:3499-3507

O8b_injection_room.sibling: query parameters emitted as JS via a hand-built string instead of JSON.stringify
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Parameters (e.g. view definitions for typeorm_metadata) sit next to the query text; a maintainer could have hand-quoted them like the query text.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: migration name inserted into `name = '...'` without quoting; camelCase (src/util/StringUtils.ts:11-17) keeps quote characters
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Name comes from the CLI path today; a planted variant taking the name from DB metadata or config would be a plausible feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted 'export schema log as script' option that emits the same queries into a JS/TS file through a separate template
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: schema:log already consumes the same schema-builder output; a second code emitter in another command would be a real second implementation at distance.

O9_family: code injection into generated source (CWE-94), improper escaping for JS template-literal context

services: cockroachdb (fix test uses these; unit-level test with stubbed schema builder possible with sqlite or no DB)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Also escape `${` but not backslashes first (or escape in the wrong order), leaving `\${` able to unescape and interpolate.

out_of_scope_notes: MigrationCreateCommand/MigrationGenerateCommand insert the CLI-path-derived name unquoted into generated class/name (src/commands/MigrationCreateCommand.ts:89-92); developer-controlled input, not this advisory's trust boundary.
unverified: Whether any non-CLI public API emits migration source was checked only by grepping src for 'implements MigrationInterface' and 'queryRunner.query(`'; none found besides the two commands.
